grep of tests/ found no test references to momentum_signals or mean_reversion_signals: the two signal functions have no unit tests asserting their intended semantics, which is why the defect was never caught.
unverified: The cost-robustness classification is not informative about a momentum edge because the as-implemented signal is a static position; no conclusion about a genuine short-horizon momentum timing strategy's cost robustness can be drawn from this activation.

The prior momentum evidence chain (37318950814 SUPPORTED, 37361000967 lookback-robust, 37394344201 horizon-stable) is confounded by this defect: the identical medians across lookbacks 3/5/10 and across horizons 20/60 are the signature of a lookback-invariant static long, not of horizon-robust momentum. Those conclusions were not re-derived here and should be treated as UNVERIFIED until the signal is repaired and re-run.
The mean-reversion FALSIFIED result (37263008074) is explained by the mirror-image static-short defect (a static short loses to the equity risk premium); it was not re-derived here.

The coin-flip null is not turnover-matched (it changes position ~112/yr vs the candidate's ~0.1/yr), so the framework's null comparison is not a like-for-like cost benchmark; this is recorded as a methodology limitation, not resolved.

observed_effect: The bounded cost check ran cleanly, reproduced exactly under an independent path, and classified the as-implemented signal COST_ROBUST at all three lookbacks — but the same run showed the candidate never changes direction (30/30 asset-lookback cells are static positions, ~0.1 sign changes/yr), so cost sensitivity is vacuous for it. The decisive effect is not the cost classification but the discovery that the 'momentum' signal thresholds mean log price rather than a return, making the entire prior momentum evidence chain a static-long equity-premium result rather than a momentum anomaly.
uncertainty_targeted: Whether the short-horizon momentum edge survives conservative transaction-cost stress on the collected real-data universe.
uncertainty_reduced: Substantially, but by redirecting the question rather than answering it as posed. Established with reproducible, independently verified evidence that (a) the as-implemented momentum signal is a static long with ~0.1 sign changes/yr, so its cost robustness is trivially COST_ROBUST and not evidence about momentum; and (b) the prior momentum 'SUPPORTED / lookback-robust / horizon-stable' results are confounded by this implementation defect. The uncertainty about 'does momentum survive costs' is now replaced by the better-posed uncertainty 'does a correctly implemented short-horizon momentum signal exist and survive costs'.
research_result: The cost-robustness question could not be answered as posed because the signal under test does not implement momentum. Evidence: (1) momentum_signals and mean_reversion_signals both compute ret = mean(log(closes[i-lookback+1:i+1])) and threshold its sign; for any series priced above 1 that quantity is positive at every bar, so momentum is a constant +1 (static long) and reversal a constant -1 (static short). (2) diag_momentum_signal.py: AAPL/AMZN/JPM at lookbacks 3/5/10 show ~4455-4462 active bars, positive=all, negative=0, exactly 1 sign change over ~17 years; sign agreement with the intended trailing-return direction is 0.536-0.604 (≈ base rate); mean-log-price quantity is positive 100% of the time. (3) The cost grid reproduces this: per-asset segment medians are identical across lookbacks 3/5/10 and essentially unchanged from 0.0x to 2.0x costs (AAPL +0.070, AMZN +0.076, JPM +0.083), because there is almost no turnover to charge; only NVDA flips negative at 5.0x. (4) The framework REGIME_STABLE count rises 6->7->8 as costs rise, which is a null-collapse artifact (the coin-flip null's ~112 changes/yr is devastated by costs), confirming that the framework verdict must not be read as edge evidence under costs. Independent verification: all five gates MATCH, including a fresh walk_forward + noise_benchmark path that reproduces every AMZN/JPM cand and null median, and a zero-cost cross-check that reproduces momentum_lookback_sweep_results.json exactly. Conclusion: the as-implemented candidate is COST_ROBUST but the classification is vacuous; the prior momentum evidence is confounded by a signal-construction defect and must not be treated as a momentum anomaly. This is durable, verified negative evidence with a precise, reproducible root cause.
